note: P4401 (Pro 31:30-31) — charm is deceitful and beauty vain, but a God-fearing woman is to be praised. Two verses; the book's close.

dims.v: fleeting allure — charm and beauty, deceptive and vain, not the ground of praise
the charm that is deceitful and the beauty that is vain — the fleeting, deceptive allure that passes and cannot bear the weight of praise, set against the enduring worth of the fear of the LORD
the fear of the LORD it is set against (267462)
set against the God-fearing worth that alone deserves praise

chen (charm/grace) — 'CHARM is deceitful, and beauty is vain' (31:30); outward attractiveness deceives and fades. It is not the measure of a woman's worth — the acrostic's whole portrait has been of character, not looks. What passes cannot ground true praise.
reverent awe — the God-fearing woman who alone is to be praised

the fear of the LORD in the woman who is to be praised — the reverent awe of God that is the root of all the strength, wisdom, kindness, and excellence the acrostic has celebrated, the enduring worth that outlasts charm and beauty and alone deserves praise
the deceptive charm it is set against (267457)
set against the fleeting allure it surpasses

yare (fear) — 'but a woman who FEARS the LORD is to be praised' (31:30); the summit and root of it all. The whole portrait rests here — the fear of the LORD is the source of her every virtue, closing the book where it began (1:7). This, not charm, is the ground of true praise.
deeds as testimony — let her own works commend her in the gates

the praising of the excellent wife by her own works in the gates — the public testimony of a life's deeds, which speak for themselves and commend her before all, so that her actions are her honour and her reward is the fruit of her own hands
the life-testimony of deeds that commend her before all

halal (praise) — 'let her WORKS praise her in the gates' (31:31); the book closes by letting her deeds speak. A tried character needs no other advocate — her works are her testimony and her honour, earning public praise where the elders sit. So Proverbs ends: character, rooted in the fear of the LORD, vindicated by its fruit.
